subject: Decision Making
title: Loss Framing in Nudges
description: A short lesson to help you apply Loss Framing in Nudges.

hook.text: A sign saying 'You lose $400 a year without insulation' works better than 'Save $400 a year with insulation.' Same.

buildup.text: Loss framing taps into loss aversion. People react more strongly to losing something than to gaining the same thing.

discovery.text: Teachers given a bonus upfront that they had to return if students failed outperformed teachers promised the same bonus.

twist.text: Energy reports showing you use more than your neighbors reduce consumption.

climax.text: Loss framing is powerful but risky. Overuse creates anxiety. The best nudges balance motivation with wellbeing.

punchline.text: Lose $400 hits harder than save $400. Loss frames move people faster.

quiz.question: Why does loss framing work as a nudge?
options: People react more strongly to potential losses than to equivalent gains
